Senses.PreferredTarget: to make a ritual bow or prostration
Senses.Explanation: The graphs join rite or reverence (禮) to bowing or obeisance (拜): to bow or prostrate oneself. The word occurs 9,933 times across 403 allowlisted texts. Chan records keep that bodily act visible while placing it at many turns of a public encounter. Xuefeng Yicun bows when he awakens at Yantou Quanhuo's words; Deshan Xuanjian bows after Longtan Chongxin blows out the paper lamp; and a later retelling preserves Deshan's earlier parting salute, return, awakening, and bow as one sequence. Mazu Daoyi challenges Preacher Liang's bow by asking what he is bowing for. Unnamed monks bow before Deshan Xuanjian, Zhaozhou Congshen, Baizhang Huaihai, Xuedou Chongxian, Hanxiu Rugan, and Zhangjing Huaihui: Deshan or Baizhang may strike, Zhaozhou may call the monk back, Hanxiu may continue speaking, or another recipient may simply receive the gesture. A commander bows and takes Yunju Daoying as teacher; an emperor bows to Baoci Guangyun and asks another question. Six unnamed followers bow and make the hands-folded greeting before Bodhidharma. The ordinary gesture thus becomes observable public-interview choreography: it can follow an answer or awakening, precede a request to speak, close a turn, return someone to the assembly, or establish a bond between instructor and student. These different actors and consequences do not change what the bow is, and the entry assigns it no unstated intent.
Senses.Note: Noun and verb frames denote the same ritual bodily action, not different things. Actor, recipient, rank, and narrative consequence likewise do not create separate senses. Fourteen witnesses preserve thirteen exact bare-headword deployments plus one explicitly marked family contrast. Compare the hands-folded greeting (問訊), parting salute (珍重), and head-to-the-ground bow (頂禮), as well as the following actions 'thereupon struck' (便打) and 'thereupon used the staff' (便棒).

Occurrences.Kwic: 言下大悟，便禮拜，起來連聲云
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall (祖堂集), Yantou Quanhuo section. Xuefeng Yicun is the exact bower: at Yantou's words he has a great awakening, bows, rises, and speaks. Yantou is the respondent and section subject, not the actor of the bow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 豁然大悟禮拜。祖云。遮鈍根阿師禮拜作麼

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: Preacher Liang, whose personal name is recorded only as Liang

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Mazu Daoyi section. Preacher Liang, whose personal name remains unnamed beyond Liang after all six attribution rungs and parallel versions, is the exact bower; Mazu Daoyi is the respondent who asks what he is bowing for.

The Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall (祖堂集), Deshan Xuanjian section. An unnamed monk is the exact bower; all six rungs leave him unnamed. Deshan Xuanjian is the respondent and following striker, not the bower.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師便禮拜。潭云：「見什摩道理？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall (祖堂集), Deshan Xuanjian section. Deshan Xuanjian is the exact bower after Longtan Chongxin blows out the light; Longtan then asks what principle Deshan saw.

Occurrences.Kwic: 其僧禮拜而退師云且來且來
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Zhaozhou Congshen section. An unnamed monk is the exact bower who withdraws; all six rungs and parallel recensions leave him unnamed. Zhaozhou Congshen calls him back.

ActorAttribution.ActorRole: bower who takes the recipient as teacher

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall (祖堂集), Yunju Daoying section. An unnamed army commander is the exact bower and takes Yunju as teacher; all six attribution rungs leave the commander personally unnamed. Yunju Daoying is the recipient and respondent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 皇帝便禮拜。皇帝又別問
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall (祖堂集), Baoci Guangyun section. The source identifies the exact bower only as an unnamed emperor after all six rungs; he bows and asks another question. Baoci Guangyun is the recipient and respondent and is not yet on the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧禮拜歸眾。乃云：「喜鵲簷前噪
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hanxiu (憨休禪師語錄), Hanxiu Rugan's own record. An unnamed monk is the exact bower who returns to the assembly; all six rungs leave him unnamed. Hanxiu Rugan is the respondent and following speaker.

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: unnamed monk sent by Baizhang Huaihai

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall (祖堂集), Baizhang Huaihai section. An unnamed monk sent by Baizhang is the exact bower and sandal-taker; all six rungs leave him unnamed. Zhangjing Huaihui is the bow recipient and respondent; Baizhang is the instructor and section subject.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是奇特事師云獨坐大雄峯僧禮拜師便打
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Baizhang Huaihai's recorded sayings. An unnamed monk asks about the extraordinary matter and bows; all six rungs leave him unnamed. Baizhang answers and is the exact following striker, anchoring ‘thereupon struck’ (便打) without confusing him with the bower.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有僧出禮拜起曰。請師答話。師便棒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Xuedou Chongxian section under the heirs of Zhimen Guangzuo. An unnamed monk is the exact bower who rises and requests an answer; all six rungs leave him unnamed. Xuedou Chongxian is the respondent and following staff actor, anchoring ‘thereupon used the staff’ (便棒).

Occurrences.Kwic: 即至祖所。禮拜問訊。祖曰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Bodhidharma section. The preceding lines identify the actors collectively as six followers but leave all six personally unnamed after the attribution ladder. They jointly bow and make the hands-folded greeting (問訊) before Bodhidharma, who is recipient and respondent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 周珍重便出，卻回曰：『外面黑。』潭點紙燈度與，周擬接，潭復吹滅，周於此大悟，便禮拜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Poshan Haiming's Recorded Sayings (破山禪師語錄), where Poshan raises the older Deshan-Longtan case. Deshan Xuanjian, called Zhou in the passage, is the exact actor who gives the parting salute (珍重), returns, awakens, and bows. Longtan Chongxin is the respondent; Poshan Haiming is the later raiser, not the bower.

The Collection from the Patriarchs' Hall (祖堂集), Bodhidharma section. Huike is the exact actor of the explicitly stronger family expression ‘head-to-the-ground bow’ (頂禮), bowing his head to the ground before attending Bodhidharma for nine years. This is a contrast-family anchor and does not buy bare-headword depth.
